reviews.text: GMX is a decentralized perpetuals exchange on Arbitrum and Avalanche. Launched in 2021, it uses GLP pools. In 2025, V2 introduced oracle upgrades. Generates revenue for stakers.

GMX is a decentralized derivatives exchange for perpetual futures (on Arbitrum, Avalanche, and Solana as of March 2025). It lets you trade crypto margined contracts up to 100x. Trading is supported by a unique multi-asset pool that earns liquidity providers fees from market making, swap fees, leverage trading and asset rebalancing. Dynamic pricing is supported by Chainlink Oracles along with TWAP pricing from leading volume DEXs. Unlike an order book, GMX uses liquidity pools (GLP) for pricing. In easy words it’s roughly an Uniswap of perpetuals.

GMX has impressed me with how deep its liquidity is. It’s a decentralized perpetual exchange that supports huge trades with almost no price impact, thanks to its unique GLP liquidity pool model. I appreciate that liquidity providers deposit single sided assets and don’t suffer impermanent loss. It’s a strong design. The downside is that it only lists major assets ETH BTC etc and has never been through a true bull market. If markets become very bullish, it’s unclear if its fee structure will be enough to incentivize LPs long term. Also, the list of tradable tokens is small by design.

After checking out GMX, my honest take is that it’s a solid decentralized exchange (DEX) for spot and perpetual contract trading. It offers low fees, minimal slippage, and allows users to trade with leverage on Arbitrum and Avalanche. It’s a great platform for advanced traders, but leverage trading can be risky, and it doesn’t offer as many pairs as centralized exchanges.
